results.caption: Show Direction
results.help_summary: The Show Line Direction Options command shows the direction (plan and 3D view) of selected lines. It does not require a command to be open to operate. The command is used to turn direction arrows on and off, and set their color and size.

results.caption: Reverse
results.help_summary: The Reverse Lines command enables you to reverse multiple linear objects at the same time.

results.caption: Set Direction
results.help_summary: The Set Line Direction command enables you to pick a reference line/alignment, then select linestrings that it will switch to run the same direction as the reference.

results.caption: Polyline
results.help_summary: Use the Create Polyline command to create a multi-segment line at a constant elevation by either picking each segment's start and end points or by streaming points. (To create a linestring that has multiple elevations, see Create and Edit a Linestring.)

results.caption: Linestring
results.help_summary: Create linestrings (versatile single or multi-segmented linear or curvilinear objects) to represent 2D or 3D linear objects. 3D lines can be defined and queried entirely from within the Plan View, and they provide a unique and versatile way of establishing the line's elevation or its vertical alignment. You can create linestrings in this software, or you can convert imported lines, such as CAD pol

results.caption: Boundary
results.help_summary: - Create a 2D boundary to delineate a portion of a surface. This is useful if you do not want to send an entire surface to field device firmware; it enables you to include a smaller surface model with your design data. The boundary clips the surface to include only the surface triangles encompassed or crossed by the boundary.

results.caption: Breakline
results.help_title: Edit a Surface by Creating a Breakline
results.help_summary: 3D lines of several types can be designated as members of a surface. They serve to influence the shape of that surface by acting in the classic manner as breaklines. These lines can exhibit complex curvilinear geometry and still serve a breaklines, by employing the breakline approximation parameters as defined in the computational settings for a surface in the Project Settings dialog.

results.caption: Polygon
results.help_summary: Create polygons to represent 2D or 3D polygonal objects that display in the graphic views. You can create polygons in the software, or you can convert imported polygons, such as CAD polygons and polygon features, and edit as necessary. To create a polygon, you specify the location of each point in the polygon and how the border line segments between them are formed (see note). You also specify the

results.caption: Outline
results.help_title: Capture Outlines from Measured or Scanned Points
results.help_summary: Capture Outlines from Measured or Scanned Points

results.caption: Create Circle
results.help_summary: Use the Create Circle command to draw a 360° arc at a constant elevation. Using the auto-advance mode, you can quickly create multiple circles with the same radius. Once created, circles can also be copied, moved, or scaled.

results.caption: Three-Point Circle
results.help_title: Create a Circle from Three Points
results.help_summary: Use the Create Three-Point Circle command to create a circle by selecting three points and/or coordinates on its circumference. This is especially useful when working with point clouds where you can use a limit box or cutting plane to specify a cross-section of a cylindrical object (for example, a tree trunk or light pole) and then select three points on the circumference to generate the circle. T

results.caption: Arc
results.help_summary: Use the Create Arc command to create an arc at a constant elevation using various creation options. The positive direction for creating an arc (using any of the options) is clockwise.

results.caption: Chord
results.help_summary: The Create Chord Lines command enables you to select one or more linestrings and set a chord distance to create individual line segments at that length, to be applied in 2D or 3D from the start of the line.

results.caption: Rectangle
results.help_summary: Use the Create Rectangle command to quickly draw rectangular polylines. Using the auto-advance mode, you can quickly create multiple rectangles. Once created, rectangles can also be copied, moved, or scaled.

results.caption: Three-Point Rectangle
results.help_title: Create a Rectangle from Three Points
results.help_summary: Use the Create Three-Point Rectangle command to create a rectangle by selecting three points and/or coordinates. Two points define the corners for one side of the rectangle; the third point defines where to draw the opposite side of the rectangle. This is especially useful when working with point clouds where you can use a limit box or cutting plane to specify a cross-section of an object (for exa

results.caption: Best-Fit Line
results.help_summary: Use the Best-Fit Line command to automatically create a straight or curved "best-fit" line based on the 2D or 3D survey, CAD, and/or scan points you select. This can be helpful, for example, when working with point clouds and creating curb and gutter linework.

results.caption: Best Fit Circle
results.help_summary: Create Best Fit Circle enables you to select at least 3 points and fit a circle using the least squares method. A preview is available to check the resulting delta values from the original points to the created circle.

results.caption: To Linestring
results.help_summary: Convert to Linestring enables you to convert alignments, polylines, and CAD line objects into Linestring objects. Additionally, it enables you to remove UCS (User Defined Coordinate Systems) from imported CAD objects or from objects created using the Cutting Plane View in TBC.
fields: Auto convert to linestrings on import [bool]

results.caption: To Horizontal
results.help_summary: The Convert to Horizontal Linestring command enables you to convert linestrings containing vertical data to horizontal data only, by linearising curves using a chord to arc tolerance. It will also add the calculated height at "?" values to the linestring.

results.caption: To Polygon
results.help_summary: Convert to Polygon enables you to convert closed CAD polylines and Linestrings into Polygons. This command converts horizontal and vertical arc data to straight line segments in the process.

results.caption: Offset
results.help_summary: Use the Offset Line command to create a new linestring offset at a specified distance from an existing line. The line from which you are offsetting can be either 2D (such as a boundary, polyline, circle, or an alignment without a vertical alignment (VAL)) or 3D (such as a 3d linestring or an alignment with a VAL). In addition, the offset can be horizontal, vertical, or both. Line segments offset f

results.caption: Variable Offset
results.help_title: Offset a Line to Variable Distances
results.help_summary: Use the Variable Offset Line command to create a linestring offset at varied distances from an existing line. The line from which you are offsetting can be either 2D or 3D with an elevation or slope.

results.caption: Move
results.help_summary: The Move Line command enables you to select a line or multiple lines and move them without needing to copy and offset.

results.caption: Merge
results.help_summary: The Merge Lines command enables you to select one linestring and a new linestring, then remove the section of the original line where the new line is located.

results.caption: Append Tracked
results.help_title: Create Linestring Segments from a Tracked Line
results.help_summary: Create Linestring Segments from a Tracked Line

results.caption: Fillet Chamfer
results.help_summary: Use the Fillet/Chamfer command to create a fillet line segment or chamfer line segment for two non-parallel line or arc segments.

results.caption: Trim Extend
results.help_summary: - Lengthen (1 below) or shorten (2) selected lines to their planimetric intersection with a specified bounding line (in yellow).

results.caption: Extend to Surface
results.help_summary: The Extend Lines to Surface command enables you to select one or multiple lines and extend them on grade to intersect a surface, extend to a set Elevation, or extend by a slope distance.

results.caption: Divide Lines
results.help_title: Divide an Existing Line into Multiple Segments
results.help_summary: Divide an Existing Line into Multiple Segments
fields: Divide by number of separated objects [radio]

results.caption: Break
results.help_summary: Break a line to split it into two separate linestrings at the point you specify. The linestrings remain coincidental at the break point, but must be edited separately thereafter.

results.caption: Explode Lines
results.help_summary: The Explode Lines command enables you to explode any linework into ether all segment elements or segments based on user defined deflection angle.

results.caption: Join
results.help_summary: Join two or more contiguous lines into individual linestrings using manual and automated methods. When lines are joined, they are converted into linestrings, thereby increasing their versatility. The resulting linestring's direction and properties are determined by the first (base) line that you choose.

results.caption: Clip
results.help_title: Clip Lines or Break Lines at Bounding Lines
results.help_summary: Clip Lines or Break Lines at Bounding Lines

results.caption: Insert/Delete Nodes
results.help_summary: The Insert/Delete Nodes command enables you to adjust linestring geometry by inserting and deleting nodes at defined locations.

results.caption: Insert Segment
results.help_title: Insert a Segment into a Linestring or Polyline
results.help_summary: Insert a Segment into a Linestring or Polyline

results.caption: Segment Count
results.help_summary: The Segment Count command enables you to count the total number of horizontal segments in the selected lines. This is useful for checking the segment numbers of avoidance zone polygons, which have a maximum number allowed in Earthworks machines.

results.caption: Delete
results.help_summary: Delete a segment from a multi-segmented line or linestring to form one or two linestrings, depending on whether you delete an interior or an end segment. If a line consists of only one segment, the entire line will be deleted. When you delete a segment from a closed shape, the remaining segments stay joined as a single line.

results.caption: Simplify
results.help_summary: The Simplify Linestrings command enables you to select one or more lines to remove unnecessary segments from the lines, and convert horizontally chorded linework to curvilinear linestrings. This is ideal for converting segmented road centerlines into true arc geometry so you can make a clean alignment string.

results.caption: Insert Vertices
results.help_summary: The Insert Vertices from Points command enables you to select a line and some points to create new vertices (and optionally, points) from points. Depending on the mode selected, the new nodes are created on the line perpendicular to the selected points, or the line is moved to the selected points.

results.caption: Integrate to Geometry
results.help_summary: Use the Integrate Points into Geometry command to automatically convert vertex coordinates for linestring-based polygonal objects and COGO parcels into points.

results.caption: Unlink
results.help_summary: The Unlink Linestrings command enables you to convert a linestring using Point IDs for its location into a coordinate-based linestring.

results.caption: Edit Elevation
results.help_summary: The Edit Linestring Elevation command enables you to select a linestring, optionally nominate beginning and end chainages, and select one of three modes (none, constant, interpolate) to edit the elevations within that chainage range.

results.caption: Set Line Elevation
results.help_summary: Apply a single, constant elevation to a 2D line to make it a 3D linestring. You can also specify a vertical offset from the elevation that you enter and a surface to which the linestring will be added.

results.caption: Adjust Profile
results.help_summary: The Adjust Profile command allows you to select one or many linestrings and apply a vertical adjustment to the profile of the string using serval different methods. This command is particularly useful for creating new strings allowing for Hog adjustment in bridge decks.

results.caption: Node Cleanup
results.help_summary: The Line Node Cleanup command enables you to clean up duplicate nodes on a linestring, adjust vertical segments, and remove node heights outside the set range.

results.caption: Compare Lines
results.help_summary: The Compare Lines command enables you to select original line data and compare it to an imported file to find linework that does not have an identical match. This is useful when receiving revisions of data, to be able to find what has changed and separate it.

results.caption: Inspect Line Nodes
results.help_summary: The Inspect Line Nodes command enables you to select a line and report the elevation, chainage, azimuth, and grades for all the nodes along the line. Annotate results to a text layer and create an Excel report.

results.caption: Check Deflections
results.help_summary: The Check Line Deflections command enables you to search selected lines to find and highlight nodes that exceed a chosen deflection angle. Use this command to find string errors before sending data to the field, or to display deflections as text on screen.

results.caption: Adjust Area
results.help_summary: The Adjust Area command enables you to place a new line or polygon that creates a boundary area equal to a value specified. It requires a selection of at least three source lines and a reference line to calculate.

results.caption: Divide Area
results.help_summary: Use the Divide Area command to divide the area in a linestring-based polygonal feature into subareas based on any of the following criteria:

results.caption: Composite Geometry
results.help_summary: Use the Create Composite Geometry command to combine simpler geometry objects, such as lines and/or polygons, into a single multipart geometric object used to represent complex spatial features, including objects with "holes" through them, such as bridges and archways.

results.caption: Track Region
results.help_title: Find the Outline of a Region
results.help_summary: Use the Track Region Outline command to create a 2D or 3D linestring representing the 2D outline of a region from a set of separate (potentially unconnected) lines and/or surface and site improvement edges. The region is derived from portions of the bounding lines/edges that planimetrically intersect (in Plan View) to form an enclosing region surrounding an interior 'seed' point. The region’s area

results.caption: Detect Crossing Geometry
results.help_title: Detect and Report on Crossing Geometry
results.help_summary: Use the Detect Crossing Geometry command to identify where lines cross planimetrically (same X and Y coordinate, but at potentially different Z levels, including self-intersecting geometry) and generate a list of the crossings. Crossings can also include end points of lines that fall planimetrically along another object or two end points at the same coordinate. The command detects intersections of
fields: Exclude objects with undefined or 0 elevations [bool]

results.caption: Create XLines
results.help_summary: The Create X Lines command enables you to select a control line and create perpendicular lines at nominated intervals and user defined locations. Nominate the width of the X line either side of the control line, or use secondary lines to control the width. Create points and lines at defined positions along the X lines.
